findings.title: Fresh installations bypass the GitHub installer identity check
findings.body: When no Integration row exists yet, this immediately advances the generic installation pipeline without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the GitHub App installation sender. Webhook delivery and the browser setup redirect are asynchronous, so a legitimate newly-created installation can reach this branch before its installation webhook has created the Integration row. An attacker who supplies such an installation ID can therefore link the app installation to their Sentry organization after authorizing their own GitHub account, which is precisely the mismatch this flow is intended to prevent. The pipeline must wait for/obtain a trusted installer identity before creating or linking an unknown installation, rather than treating a missing Integration as verified.

findings.title: Missing webhook sender metadata crashes the setup flow
findings.body: This direct nested lookup raises KeyError/TypeError when an existing Integration has no `metadata.sender` or a sender without a `login`, producing a 500 instead of the installation failure page. Integrations created by the normal pipeline do not populate `sender` (the basic-flow test asserts metadata without it), and older or partially-cleaned-up Integration rows can also reach the explicitly supported state where the Integration exists but no OrganizationIntegration does. Handle absent/malformed sender metadata as an unverifiable installation (or migrate it) before attempting the comparison.

findings.title: OAuth provider failures escape as server errors
findings.body: Only decoding/parsing `safe_urlread` is wrapped in the try block. `safe_urlopen` itself can raise for token-endpoint HTTP/network failures, and `get_user_info` after the block can raise for a rejected token or GitHub API failure. Those cases bypass `error()` and return a 500, rather than the invalid-installation response promised by this flow. Catch the provider/API exceptions around both the token exchange and user lookup and render the failure response.
